title: GLaVis: Generative Latent Visual Queries for Multimodal Conversational Recommender Systems with MLLMs

problem.claim: Multimodal conversational recommender systems aim to capture user preferences expressed across diverse modalities and multi-turn interactions.

gap.claim: Existing MLLM-based approaches are constrained either by reliance on external retrievers or by information bottlenecks caused by translating visual intents into intermediate text.

contributions.claim: GLaVis is an end-to-end generative visual retrieval framework that enables an MLLM to produce continuous latent embeddings as visual queries for multimodal conversational recommendation.
A lightweight visual query projector maps MLLM hidden states into the visual embedding space using a reason-before-generation approach.
A multi-stage training strategy combines supervised-fine-tuning meta-alignment with GRPO-based task-oriented reinforcement learning to jointly optimize visual alignment and response generation.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on two public datasets, MMD and FashionRec, reportedly show that GLaVis significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in visual recommendation accuracy and response quality.
The authors report that the code is available on GitHub.

narrative_sequence.summary: MCRSs seek to capture multimodal and multi-turn user preferences.
Existing MLLM-based paradigms face retriever dependence or textual information bottlenecks.
GLaVis directly generates continuous latent visual queries, supported by a visual query projector and reason-before-generation process.
Multi-stage training jointly addresses visual alignment and natural-language response generation.
The authors report improvements over state-of-the-art baselines on two public datasets and provide a code link.

source_observation.claim: The framework generates continuous latent visual queries directly from an MLLM rather than translating visual intent into intermediate text.

interpretation.claim: Direct representation-space interaction may reduce information loss introduced by textual intermediates.

application.claim: For multimodal systems, consider connecting language-model representations directly to the target modality's embedding space.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish when direct latent querying is preferable to external retrieval or textual interfaces.

unknowns: The abstract does not provide dataset sizes, splits, evaluation metrics, or numerical results.
The abstract does not identify the compared baselines or quantify the reported improvements.
The abstract does not describe the model architecture, training stages, or GRPO configuration in sufficient detail.
